name: Saudi Arabia

income_tax.summary: There is no individual income tax scheme in Saudi Arabia; employment income is untaxed (PwC, reviewed 29 Jul 2026). Non-employment income is taxed under entity/permanent-establishment rules. Non-Saudi employees pay no GOSI contribution (the 2% occupational-hazard charge is borne by the employer); Saudi employees pay 9.75% (9% plus 0.75% SANED).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed contributions not covered by PwC. A freelancer's non-employment income can fall under the entity (corporate) rules rather than personal tax; the 20% foreign-owned profit tax is noted in the existing jurisdiction file.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income-based taxes. Saudi employees' GOSI base is basic salary plus housing, capped at SAR 45,000 a month.

open_questions: How a foreign freelancer's self-employment income is taxed in practice (entity rules) is not detailed on the PwC page.

PwC other-taxes page re-opened 2026-10-15: non-Saudi employees 2% (employer-paid occupational hazard only), Saudi employees 9.75% employee share; no self-employed rate listed (0% is a reading of silence).

residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: no visa-free right to work. Skilled employees are sponsored by a Saudi employer for an iqama (residence and work permit). Premium Residency for wealthy foreigners is noted in the existing jurisdiction file. No dedicated digital-nomad visa was found.
open_questions: No digital-nomad visa found; not confirmed from an official source.
Premium Residency terms and employer-sponsorship rules not re-verified.
